question: Will this project hand over within 6 months of the first handover date we have on record?

rules.closed: a project whose first handover is more than 6 months in the past (month now minus first handover > 6)
rules.on_time: a closed project marked completed whose recorded date moves add up to 6 months or less
rules.comparables: closed projects in the same market if there are at least 10, else in the same country if at least 10, else not enough comparable projects (the pooled figure over all markets is then shown only as context)

status.open: not completed, first handover less than 6 months ago or still ahead, and the advertised date has not moved more than 6 months: estimated
status.missed: not completed and more than 6 months past the first handover: already answered, no
status.moved: not completed and the developer's own current date is more than 6 months after the first one: no, unless it hands over earlier than it now says
status.done_on_time: completed, recorded moves of 6 months or less
status.done_late: completed, recorded moves of more than 6 months
status.no_date: no handover date in the open data
status.completed_no_date: completed, no date in the open data
status.inconsistent: a past handover year but no overdue reading: left out until the research agent re-reads it

why_not_stage: The brief for this estimate asked to match on stage and on months to the promised date. The open data has no dated record of what stage each closed project was at, or when its delay was announced, so matching on today's stage would be circular (a project that handed over is "completed" because of the outcome). The monthly snapshot below records stage, advertised date and moves for every project from November 2026, so comparables can be matched on stage and time to handover once those snapshots have closed windows.
bias: The tracked projects are the ones being marketed now. Projects that handed over on time and stopped marketing are less likely to be in the data, so the on-time rate among closed projects is very likely lower than the true rate. Treat it as a floor for what this data set shows, not as a forecast.

validation.method: Leave one out: for each project whose window has closed, the estimate is recomputed from all other closed projects with the same rule, then compared with what happened.
validation.verdict: With 47 closed cases and no market reaching 10, every back-test estimate falls back to the pooled rate, so the estimate has no power to tell projects apart yet. Its calibration is only as good as the pooled rate: it matches the average by construction and says nothing about any single project.
